Explore the Modules
Immerse yourself in 6 educational modules, each building your skills progressively. Navigate various aspects of AI-assisted verification.
  • Module 1 — Verification Mindset and AI Literacy
    Introduces the foundations of AI-assisted verification and explains why journalists must treat AI as a supportive assistant rather than an autonomous decision-maker. The module establishes the core principles of verification culture, human editorial oversight, and responsible AI use in journalism.
    What You Will Learn
    • What AI-assisted verification means
    • Human-in-the-loop (HITL) verification logic
    • Differences between traditional and AI-assisted verification
    • Risks of overreliance on automation
    • Basic concepts of misinformation, disinformation, and synthetic media
    Interactive Elements
    • AI vs Human decision scenarios
    • Information disorder classification quiz
    • “Would you publish this?” branching exercise
    • Interactive newsroom dilemmas
    • Audio summaries
  • Module 2 — Smart Skepticism, Ethics, and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
    Focuses on the critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs and the ethical risks associated with automated systems. Learners explore transparency, accountability, algorithmic bias, hallucinations, privacy, and responsible newsroom practices while applying the human-in-the-loop approach to AI-assisted verification.
    What You Will Learn
    • How AI hallucinations occur
    • Bias and transparency problems in AI systems
    • Ethical risks in automated journalism
    • Privacy and accountability concerns
    • How to critically interpret AI-generated outputs
    • Why human editorial oversight remains essential
    Interactive Elements
    • Hallucinated source detection activity
    • Bias recognition scenarios
    • Ethical newsroom simulations
    • Transparency checklist exercises
    • Human-in-the-loop decision tasks
    • Reflection-based mini quizzes
  • Module 3 — The Verifier’s Toolkit
    Provides a structured guide to verification tools and workflows. Instead of presenting isolated tools, the module explains which tools should be used in different verification scenarios and how they fit into newsroom workflows.
    What You Will Learn
    • Reverse image search workflows
    • Metadata and geolocation basics
    • Tool selection logic
    • Verification decision trees
    • How to combine tools effectively
    Interactive Elements
    • Tool-selection decision tree
    • Interactive verification workflow maps
    • “Choose the right tool” quiz
    • Guided tool demonstrations
    • Verification checklist downloads
  • Module 4 — Applied Text and Claim Verification
    Develops practical skills for verifying textual claims, political statements, quotations, statistics, and AI-generated text. Learners practise evidence comparison and contextual analysis through realistic newsroom cases.
    What You Will Learn
    • Claim extraction techniques
    • Source comparison methods
    • Quote and statistic verification
    • Detecting decontextualized information
    • AI-generated text analysis
    Interactive Elements
    • Real-world claim verification tasks
    • Fake vs verified comparison cards
    • AI-generated article analysis
    • Source credibility exercises
    • Interactive newsroom case studies
  • Module 5 — Visual, Video, and Deepfake Verification
    Focuses on visual verification techniques for images, videos, and synthetic media. Learners investigate metadata, keyframes, deepfake indicators, and multimodal manipulation strategies.
    What You Will Learn
    • Reverse image search methods
    • Video keyframe extraction
    • Deepfake warning signs
    • Metadata interpretation
    • Geolocation and visual cross-checking
    Interactive Elements
    • Deepfake detection checklist
    • Keyframe investigation exercises
    • Image verification challenges
    • Metadata analysis simulations
    • Interactive visual comparison tasks
  • Module 6 — Integrated Workflow Scenarios
    Combines all previous modules into realistic newsroom simulations. Learners complete multimodal verification tasks under professional constraints, including uncertainty management and editorial decision-making.
    What You Will Learn
    • End-to-end verification workflows
    • Multimodal investigation strategies
    • Editorial uncertainty reporting
    • Workflow integration under time pressure
    • Professional verification documentation
    Interactive Elements
    • Full newsroom verification simulation
    • Multimodal breaking news exercises
    • Deadline-pressure scenarios
    • Editorial decision exercises
    • Final capstone assessment
